text:
sam: Quick coordination call — I want to pilot two runtime tweaks on redwood-13b-v1 tonight: enable speculative decoding and bump KV prefetch window from 8 -> 12 for a small canary. Goal is to shave tail latency on long sequences without degrading quality. Planning: 3% audience for 2 hours, evaluate latency/quality, then 10% if ok. Any blockers?

tara: +1 on the experiment. two quick asks: 1) split canary by request-length buckets (short <512, long >=512) so we can see signal separately; 2) ensure fallback guardrail to disable speculative decoding if p95 increases >20ms or quality regressions detected.

nisha: Also want a baseline eval on our standard prompt-suite before/after. I'll run an automated eval job as soon as the canary starts. If you want, I can subscribe the eval job to the canary audience so results come in real-time.

sam: good call on buckets. Plan: audience=3% overall but with 60% of that traffic from long-seq bucket, 40% short. Guardrail thresholds: p95 latency +20ms, top-k token-delta > 0.5% (we'll compare embedding-based similarity on 500 samples).

ken: FYI I merged the runtime toggle PR (link: https://git.redwood/repo/pull/412). No ABI changes; kernel selector picks flash-attn path if GPU supports it. Spec-decoding flag lives in config as `speculative_decode.enabled`.

dev-bot: preflight checks complete for redwood-13b-v1 canary 
- config diff: ok
- unit tests: ok
- staging benchmark: p95 down 12ms, median unchanged
- compatibility matrix: GPUs: A100v4/RTX8000 ok

sam: putting the exact commands here for ops to run (will tag ops):
```
ffctl set speculative_decode=true --model=redwood-13b-v1 --env=prod --audience=3% --buckets=short:40%,long:60% --note="spec decode + kv_window 12 canary"
ffctl set kv_prefetch_window=12 --model=redwood-13b-v1 --env=prod --audience=3%
```

tara: add a kill-switch TTL: auto-disable after 2 hours unless `canary_approve=true` is set. Also add annotation for rollback-runbook link.

nisha: I'll post the eval dashboard link once job is wired. Metrics to watch: gen_latency_p95, token_throughput, embedding_similarity_mean, customer-error-rate. I'll add a diff visualization.

ops-bot: scheduling canary per request. Next steps: 1) confirm maintenance window? 2) confirm oncall for alert thresholds?

sam: no maintenance window required, low-risk. oncall: @tara will be primary, @ken backup. I’ll run the rollout at 22:00 UTC if no objections.

ken: I'll stand by and cut a hotfix branch if we see any kernel regressions. Also recommend enabling detailed kv-cache logging for canary only: `kv.cache.debug=true` (low sample rate).

ops-bot: rollout scheduled: 22:00 UTC, audience 3% (short/long buckets). Automated guardrails: disable on p95 +20ms or embedding_similarity_mean drop >0.5%. Notifications: #eng-runtime + pager.

sam: thanks — I'll post results thread after 2h. :thumbsup:

nisha: perfect, I'll start the eval job shortly and subscribe alerts.

tara: one last note — if speculative decode reduces p95 but increases variance in small requests we should consider gating by request_size rather than blanket enable. Keep an eye on short-bucket p99.

sam: noted. will collect short/long p95/p99 and quality diffs.

ops-bot: post-rollout checklist will be automatically posted to the channel at rollout completion.

ken: good luck — ping me immediately if anything odd shows up.

sam: thanks everyone.
